areas.title: Tool task v2: nested calls, structured output, callers, modelTools and deferred tools
areas.summary: pi.tool becomes version 2: ToolTaskInput and ToolTaskResult are tagged unions of model-issued and nested calls, and version 1 tasks migrate. A running tool can call another tool through ToolExecutionApi.executeTool(); the nested call is its own pi.tool task owned by the caller, its result goes to the caller's task-scoped NestedCallDoc instead of the transcript, it shows in pi.live.nestedTools and in tool events (parentToolCallId, parentTaskId, taskId). ToolExecutionResult.content becomes output, tools can declare structuredOutputSchema and return a validated structuredOutput, ToolRegistration gains callers and deferred, and AgentState gains modelTools so Agent exposes tools, callable and deferred. bash and powershell return an error result with an exit_code diagnostic for a nonzero exit instead of throwing.

changelog.item: ToolTaskInput/ToolTaskResult are now kind-tagged unions (model or nested); pi.tool v2 migrates live v1 tasks
ToolExecutionResult.content renamed to output; new structuredOutput channel
bash/powershell report a nonzero exit as an error result with an exit_code diagnostic, not a throw
executeTool() runs a nested tool call as an owned pi.tool task; results live in NestedCallDoc, keyed for replay; shown in pi.live.nestedTools and tool events
structuredOutputSchema/structuredOutput validated by the Harness; api.retainedOutput(); bash/powershell structured output { output, truncated, fullOutputPath?, exitCode }
ToolRegistration.callers and AgentState.modelTools decide who may call a tool and what the model is offered; Agent.callable lists nested-call targets
ToolRegistration.deferred hides a tool until modelTools.add loads it (control.addTools appends); Agent.deferred lists the unloaded ones

The content->output rename touches every C# tool and almost every harness test file, and the pisharp durable CLI (area l) does not compile until it adapts, so land l right after a or adapt DurableSubagent.cs here. NestedCallDoc is a task-scoped document family (kind pi.tool.nested-call); Documents.cs already supports DocumentScopeKind.Task families. Nested slots in pi.live are found by binary search over ascending task IDs because each lookup costs a tracker node; keep that in the C# Draft API. A nested call aborted or left running when its caller settles is aborted through TaskRuntime.abortOwned/ownedTasks and gets abandonOnRestart for non-replay-safe callers, so area c must be in first. Structured output validation reuses the TypeBox-compatible validator in Internal/PiAi/Validation.cs. The record JSON changes (input.kind, result.kind, NestedCallDoc, nestedTools, ToolEventCall.taskId) must match upstream byte for byte for decision 0005 compatibility; the written compat captures for tool scenarios switch to the v1.2.0 corpus from area m here. harness/types.ts, events.ts, live.ts and generation.ts are also edited earlier by areas b, i and j; this area owns their rows because it lands last among them. nested-images-bench and scheduler-fanout-bench are here because they drive executeTool, not images or the scheduler alone.

areas.title: Storage failure, Session lifecycle and document cache retention
areas.summary: Any error a Storage method throws now fails the Session for good: it seals admission, runs close listeners, closes Storage itself, and every later call or pending wait rejects with SessionFailed (cause = the storage error). StorageRejected is removed; StorageRequestError marks an invalid read request that fails only that call. Session.closed settles with { reason: closed | failed }, WatchEnd gains session_failed, commit/close listeners that throw are reported through onReport instead of failing the operation, and onReport/now are made safe. The Session document cache becomes bounded: an unobserved document leaves memory after documentRetentionMs (default 10 minutes, 0 = right after use) and reloads from Storage.

changelog.item: A throwing Storage method fails and closes the Session; later calls reject with SessionFailed; nothing retries
StorageRejected removed; StorageRequestError fails only the invalid read
Session.closed promise and WatchEnd reason session_failed
Throwing subscribeCommits/subscribeClose listeners are reported via onReport, not propagated
onReport and now() made safe; watch listener errors are reported and end the watch
A failed fault write no longer reruns the task in the same process
Session document cache evicts unobserved documents after documentRetentionMs (HarnessSettings and createSession option)

areas.notes: Removing StorageRejected and the retry paths changes recovery semantics that crash tests and the SQLite facade rely on: a failed commit is now final and the process reopens the Session. Every Storage call goes through one guard in SessionImpl (upstream SessionImpl.storage); in C# wrap the IStorage the Harness receives, and treat OperationCanceledException from the caller's token like upstream treats a context abort (fails only that read). Retention needs a timer that does not keep the process alive and a line job for retention 0; upstream runs its whole suite a second time with retention 0, so add an equivalent pass (env var or test-runner flag) to tests/PiSharp.Durable.Tests rather than only the new retention cases. Chord replicatedState gains an onError option in area f that the view, task-graph and document-state observers use here. areas.title: Scheduler: ownership indexes, abandonOnRestart, abortOwned/ownedTasks, wait cycles
areas.summary: The scheduler stops visiting every live task per pass: an in-memory ownership index drives abort cascades (only from tasks with cancellation intent), owned-live and idle-scope walks, with separate candidate sets for reservation, finalization and failFast, and the index is bounded by live work (it forgets ended chains and reloads them from storage). TaskOptions.abandonOnRestart marks tasks whose creator awaits them only in memory; a later Harness abort-marks them with abortReason restart, cascading, before they run again. TaskRuntime gains abortOwned and ownedTasks. commit() rejects a wait that would close any wait-for cycle, and no task below an owner with cancellation intent starts a run phase.

changelog.item: TaskOptions.abandonOnRestart with abortReason restart, cascading at the next Harness start
TaskRuntime.abortOwned(id) and TaskRuntime.ownedTasks()
No run phase starts below an owner with cancellation intent
Waits closing a cycle through waits and held owners are rejected with the cycle named (#10411)
Scheduler walks an ownership index instead of all live tasks; large fan-outs and long chains settle much faster
Ownership indexes bounded by live work; queued input no longer scans all queued submissions

areas.notes: scheduler.ts is a rewrite (663+/145-); port it as a whole against the v1.2.0 text instead of patching the C# line by line, keeping the C# concurrency model (the Scheduler.cs header documents its threading). The index-size test hook (SCHEDULER_INDEX_SIZES symbol) needs an internal C# accessor (InternalsVisibleTo the test project). Wait-cycle detection reads owner chains from storage for unloaded nodes, so it is async inside commit(). abandonOnRestart and abortReason are new optional task-record fields; RecordJson must write them only when set to keep records byte-equal to upstream. harness.ts and src/types.ts carry area b changes as well; this area owns their rows because it lands after b. scheduler-fanout-bench is in area a because it needs executeTool.

areas.title: Durable code mode
areas.summary: New @earendil-works/pi-durable/codemode: a replay-safe codemode tool (createCodemodeExtension({ sandbox })) whose scripts call the conversation's tools as nested calls and survive a restart by replaying the script deterministically from a journal (pi.codemode.run, pi.codemode.journal, pi.codemode.store documents), reattaching to nested calls by key. It adds a codemode prompt section with namespaces and an inline token budget, searchTools/describeTool/describeNamespace, output layout with truncation and spill files, models.* (catalog, classify, generateImages as internal nested tools, at most four at once) and the Lark grammar for constrained sampling. Divergence, a changed sandbox fingerprint or module version, or a passed deadline ends the call with an error.

changelog.item: New codemode tool and extension: scripts call tools as nested calls and replay deterministically after a restart
codemode prompt section, script-side tool search/describe, result layout with spill and saved images, per-conversation store()/load()
models.* in scripts (catalog, classify, generateImages) run as internal nested tools

areas.notes: Sized XL although the line count says L, because the deterministic Jint runner is new C# with no upstream file in this diff. Biggest risk of the sync. Durable code mode needs pi-codemode 1.2.0's deterministic sandbox.start() (virtual clock from startedAt, Math.random from seed, UTC, no WeakRef/FinalizationRegistry, results applied in host-numbered order, onStarted fingerprint, onIdle with issued-call counts, run.deliver(), run.finished). The main-line sync (decision 0006, applicability entry codemode.new-sandboxes) EXCLUDED sandbox.start() because PiSharp runs code mode on Jint, so PiSharp.Codemode has no deterministic mode today; it has to be added to the Jint runner as an additive seam, flagged for upstreaming to main per decision 0005, with packages/codemode/test/deterministic.test.ts ported as its test. The replay guarantee depends on Jint being deterministic for the same inputs (property order, Date, Math.random, promise job order); the fingerprint must change whenever the Jint engine or prelude changes. PiSharp.Durable.Tools gains a dependency on PiSharp.Codemode (and Jint) that decision 0005 section 4 does not list; record it. models.* needs model catalog, classifier and image-generation calls that IDurableModels does not expose; bridge to PiSharp.AI ModelOperations (ClassifierShared, OpenRouterImages) or leave models.* unsupported with a recorded difference. Search.cs (rankDocuments) comes from area k. The codemode section must leave deferred tools out (area a semantics).

areas.title: Images: read returns images, image processor
areas.summary: read returns PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP files within the model's image limits (default 2000x2000 px, 4.5 MB of base64) as one image block instead of an unsupported_image error; with createCodingTools({ images }) an ImageProcessor orients, converts and shrinks them to fit, and a model without image input gets a diagnostic about the placeholder it sees. The new images entry point provides a Photon (WebAssembly) processor with EXIF orientation, plus a Node loader that prepares images in a worker thread that exits after 30 s idle. tools/image.ts gains streaming MIME detection and header dimension parsing.

changelog.item: read returns images as an image block within ImageLimits; createCodingTools({ images }) prepares them with an ImageProcessor
New images entry point: Photon processor with EXIF orientation; Node loader runs it in a worker thread

Delta tracker plans order-preserving array edits from changed ranges; applyImmutable appends with one copy (32k appends 11.3 s -> 1.4 s)

areas.title: Input entries and display-only writes

A display-only write (only kind and data, no model/head/edits) is appended and settled done at once even while the conversation is busy or has queued items, unless a queued reset would hide it.
